title: Tenant-level Egress Scoping Switch & Authorization Protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a lightweight, tenant-scoped egress authorization component ("egress scoping switch") that enforces EU-only/data-residency constraints, tenant allowlists/denylists, and tier-based routing decisions. The switch will evaluate per-request metadata, resolve tenant policy, select a permitted region + model tier, and apply fallback model variant rules when the preferred variant is unavailable. This ticket covers design, API contract for the switch, runtime admission checks, audit logging, and integration points with existing routing and policy services. Goal: provide a single, authoritative enforcement point that prevents accidental cross-border egress and centralizes tenant exceptions while preserving low-latency routing for P0/P1 customers.
acceptance_criteria: A tenant policy config format exists and supports: residency_scope (EU_ONLY|REGIONAL|GLOBAL), allowed_regions list, denied_regions list, allowed_model_tiers list, emergency_passthrough boolean, and fallback_variant_order list.

Runtime switch evaluates requests and returns one of: ALLOW(region, model_variant), DENY(reason), or SOFT_FALLBACK(region, fallback_variant) with latency < 5ms median on local bench for metadata-only decision path.
End-to-end tests covering: EU-only tenant blocked for non-EU region, tenant allowlisted for single EU region, tenant denied specific model tier and routed to lower tier as defined by fallback order.

Audit events emitted for every decision include tenant_id, resolved_policy_version, decision, reason, selected_region, selected_model_variant, and request_id; events appear in Console logs and are queryable for 90 days.
Feature toggle (runtime flag) to enable/disable enforcement per environment for staged rollout; default off in staging, on for EU customers in canary environment.
Security review completed and any KMS/HSM key usage for storing tenant policy secrets documented.
Migration plan for existing tenant exceptions: CSV importer and migration script validated on sandbox tenants.
Instrumentation: metric per-decision type and per-tenant counters, synthetic test that validates at least 3 tenants with residency policies in CI daily.
Documentation: README with config schema, operator runbook, and example tenant configs stored in Confluence linked from ticket.
No false negatives found in a 48-hour staging soak with traffic simulation against 10 representative tenant profiles.
decisions: Implement switch as a small stateless service colocated with edge routing layer to reduce RTT for decision path.
Policy storage will be versioned JSON in tenant-config DB with change-feed; switch caches policies for 30s and invalidates on change events.
Fallback resolution: prefer region-preserving fallback first (other EU regions) then tier-degradation only if regional options exhausted.
Allowlist/denylist semantics: deny takes precedence over allow; emergency_passthrough flag can override denies only with explicit audit and manual JWT claim from sales/ops.
Decisions exposed as an opaque header for downstream runtime components to act on, but not to be relied upon for security enforcement except by trusted internal runtimes.
Keep decision logic deterministic and side-effect free so it can be unit-tested and simulated in customer-facing tooling.
implementation_steps: 1) Draft config schema and update tenant-config service to persist policy JSON with schema v1.
2) Build stateless egress-scoping-switch service with REST+gRPC API: /resolve(decision_request) -> decision_response.
3) Integrate local cache with change-feed to invalidate per-tenant on policy update.
4) Add audit event emitter to central logging pipeline and wire into Console's routing audit dashboard.
5) Add runtime feature flag and deploy to canary, staging, then EU canary tenants.
6) Create migration CSV importer and run on a sandbox cluster to validate mappings.
7) Implement CI tests and synthetic traffic experiments to validate no cross-border egress.
8) Rollout to production with gradual ramp and post-rollout validation queries.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design review and security sign-off (this ticket) - enable feature flag in dev/staging.
Phase 1: Deploy switch to canary edge; run internal tenant-only traffic and assert decisions are expected (48h).
Phase 2: Enable enforcement for a small set of EU-only tenants with monitoring and manual ops guardrails (72h).
Phase 3: Expand to all EU-regulated tenants; enable audit retention and runbook.
Phase 4: Global rollout for residency-aware routing and provide opt-in for non-EU tenants.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy resolution logic covering allow/deny precedence, emergency_passthrough, and fallback orders.
Integration tests with routing layer to ensure selected region + model variant is propagated and used by runtime.
Chaos test: simulate preferred model variant OOM and assert switch selects next fallback variant and emits appropriate audit event.
Performance test: microbench decision path with cache-hit and cache-miss scenarios to ensure < 5ms median and < 20ms p95.
End-to-end compliance test: synthetic traffic from non-EU egress points rejected for EU-only tenants in staging cluster.
risks: Misconfiguration risk: incorrect policy JSON could accidentally allow cross-border egress; mitigated by schema validation and preflight checks.
Latency risk: additional hop may add RTT; mitigated by colocating with edge and aggressive caching.
Operational risk: emergency_passthrough misuse by Support - require approval workflow and audit trail.
Compatibility risk: downstream runtimes must respect headers; plan includes hard-fail mode for trusted runtimes only.
Rollback complexity if a wide policy change is applied incorrectly - mitigation: staged rollout and fast rollback script.
